source: miller_1980_tacs_jamming; fm_100_2_1_1984 ch. 15; fm_34_40_7 (the jamming rule, comms_jamming.hpp); SAM3D estimates as marked
notes: Our side's radio-electronic combat against the enemy's command in the air (roadmap S2, simcore/air_war/counter_c2.hpp, docs/air_battle/05_C2_AND_RETASKING.md section 9): each enemy post is marked to be destroyed, jammed or listened to; a post marked for destruction is struck by our fires once our listeners have heard enough of its calls to fix it; a post marked for jamming has its net jammed by our air-net jammers behind our line, judged by FM 34-40-7's J/S rule. Read by the air war's campaign and by a session's enemy radio (the jammers as EM spot jammers on the posts' nets, data/em/air_radios_1985.json 'our_air_net_jammer').

split.source: miller_1980_tacs_jamming (the Soviet plan against NATO's tactical air control: destroy a third of its command, control and communications, jam a third, listen to the rest); the post-by-post draw a SAM3D game value

df_bearing_deg.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 15-2 (Soviet VHF direction finding: bearings within 3.5 degrees)

df_reach_km.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 15-2 (VHF intercept and direction finding to about 40 km)

fires_reach_km.source: SAM3D estimate: how deep past the line the front's fires (rocket artillery, tactical missiles, the front's aviation) are laid on a located command post

enemy_set_w.source: estimate (the air sets' power in data/em/air_radios_1985.json, itself an estimate)

jammers.name: R-834-class jammer of the enemy's air-ground voice nets

band_mhz.source: estimate: the air voice bands (VHF 100-156 MHz, UHF 225-400 MHz, data/em/air_radios_1985.json); the R-834's own band is not given by a source read

power_w.source: estimate (no source read gives the R-834's power; the class of FM 34-40-7's worked examples, 1.5 kW)

behind_km.source: estimate: behind our leading troops, as the front's jamming units stood (fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 15-2 puts the intercept behind the leading regiments)

jammers.source: fm_100_2_1_1984 pp. 15-2 to 15-3 (the R-834 named among the jammers of the air-ground nets; TACS's strike control and the nets to the FACs among the targets); in service no later than that manual (1984)
